name: Education
dimension: the element of an educational arrangement

objects.label: Aims and curricula
objects.text: ED.O.A1 Aims and curricula

objects.label: Aims
objects.text: ED.O.A1.1 Aims — the stated purposes of education. The normative argument for them is PL; the statement of an adopted aim is ED (W12).

objects.label: Curriculum content
objects.text: ED.O.A1.2 Curriculum content — what is taught. The truth of the content stays with its owner (a theorem is MA).

objects.label: Sequence and progression
objects.text: ED.O.A1.3 Sequence and progression — learning progressions and prerequisites.

objects.label: National curricula
objects.text: ED.O.A1.4 National curricula — e.g. Te Whāriki (NZ early childhood) and Te Marautanga o Aotearoa (Māori-medium) as stated frameworks (W12).

objects.label: Learners
objects.text: ED.O.A2 Learners

objects.label: Prior knowledge and misconceptions
objects.text: ED.O.A2.1 Prior knowledge and misconceptions — e.g. the impetus misconception in force and motion (physics education research). The cognitive mechanism is MS.

objects.label: Development
objects.text: ED.O.A2.2 Development — age-related readiness, cited from MS.

objects.label: Motivation
objects.text: ED.O.A2.3 Motivation and engagement.

objects.label: Diversity and learning need
objects.text: ED.O.A2.4 Diversity and learning need — inclusion, special education, gifted learners.

objects.label: Teaching
objects.text: ED.O.A3 Teaching

objects.label: Instruction
objects.text: ED.O.A3.1 Instruction — explicit instruction versus discovery; worked examples help novices (an expertise-reversal effect is a stated defeater for experts).

objects.label: Feedback
objects.text: ED.O.A3.2 Feedback — effects vary widely by type; some feedback lowers performance (UNVERIFIED as a meta-analytic figure).

objects.label: Practice and retrieval
objects.text: ED.O.A3.3 Practice and retrieval — spacing and retrieval practice improve long-term retention. The memory mechanism is MS.

objects.label: Technology in teaching
objects.text: ED.O.A3.4 Technology in teaching — effects depend on use, not presence.

objects.label: Culturally sustaining pedagogy
objects.text: ED.O.A3.5 Culturally sustaining pedagogy — Kaupapa Māori education (kura kaupapa Māori) as an arrangement. The tradition-internal content is IK.

objects.label: Assessment
objects.text: ED.O.A4 Assessment

objects.label: Validity
objects.text: ED.O.A4.1 Validity — an argument that score interpretations are supported (W9 with W4).

objects.label: Reliability
objects.text: ED.O.A4.2 Reliability — score consistency; the statistics are MA.O.A5 (psychometrics as bridge).

objects.label: Formative assessment
objects.text: ED.O.A4.3 Formative assessment — assessment used to change teaching.

objects.label: High-stakes testing
objects.text: ED.O.A4.4 High-stakes testing and accountability — Campbell's law: the more a quantitative indicator drives decisions, the more it is subject to corruption pressures (stated as a tendency).

objects.label: Institutions and systems
objects.text: ED.O.A5 Institutions and systems

objects.label: Schools
objects.text: ED.O.A5.1 Schools — school effects, leadership, class size.

objects.label: School systems
objects.text: ED.O.A5.2 School systems — international comparisons (PISA, TIMSS) are W4 within their sampling designs.

objects.label: Higher education
objects.text: ED.O.A5.3 Higher education — universities, credentials.

objects.label: Equity and access
objects.text: ED.O.A5.4 Equity and access — gaps by group. The returns to schooling are EC; the law on schooling is LA.

warrants.standard: trial or identified effect, with the learners stated

sections.governing_thought:
Education is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five elements of an educational arrangement: aims and curricula, learners, teaching, assessment, and institutions and systems.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the element of an educational arrangement.** Order: from purpose to system.
1. Aims and curricula
2. Learners
3. Teaching
4. Assessment
5. Institutions and systems
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place by the element of the arrangement.
2. The truth of what is taught stays with its owner. ED owns the learning claim.
3. The mind's mechanism is MS. Its educational use is ED.
4. The economic return is EC. The legal duty is LA. The political decision is PO.
5. MSC 97 is a bridge: the mathematics is MA; learning it is ED.
6. The learning line (Phase 2.1). A claim that learners changed under a stated arrangement (teaching, curriculum, assessment, institution) is ED. A claim about how learning or memory works in any mind, with no arrangement in it, is MS.O.A1.5. Test: delete the arrangement from the sentence. If the claim survives, it is MS; if it does not, it is ED. MS.O.A1.5.5 is retired and points here.
